The core duality in StatKing's architecture lies between legal usability and data richness. The coverage gap \( \mathcal{C} \) defines the fundamental constraint: \( \mathcal{C} \) is a ratio of legally usable data to total seeded data. As \( \mathcal{C} \to 0 \), the system enters a failure mode where actionable intelligence becomes sparse. Trust and conflict metrics \( \mathcal{T} \) and \( \mathcal{F} \) form a dual axis that determines data integrity. When \( \mathcal{F} \to \infty \), trust collapses, leading to unreliable inferences. The freshness metric \( \mathcal{F}_{\text{fresh}} \) ensures that even high-quality data remains relevant over time. These primitives form a triadic kernel: \( \mathcal{C} \times \mathcal{T} \cdot \mathcal{F}^{-1} \times \mathcal{F}_{\text{fresh}} \) underpins the system’s epistemic robustness. Failure modes include data loss due to legal constraints, trust erosion from conflicting signals, and obsolescence from stale data.
